outcome: No proof, no case settled, and no improved bound on the smallest exceptional eigenvalue for congruence subgroups have appeared since 26 January 2024; the best bound remains Kim-Sarnak's 975/4096 (2003), and the live Wikipedia article (as of a July 2025 revision) still cites Kim-Sarnak as the state of the art.
summary: I found no evidence that Selberg's 1/4 conjecture (the statement that eigenvalues of the Laplace operator on Maass wave forms of congruence subgroups are at least 1/4) has been resolved, partially settled, or had its best known bound improved since 26 January 2024. The best bound remains Kim-Sarnak's 975/4096 ≈ 0.238 (2003), confirmed by the current Wikipedia article on the topic (last substantively updated per the fetch on 19 June 2025), which cites no post-2024 progress. I checked two candidate leads the triage pass had not opened: arXiv:2410.22711 turned out to concern L-functions in the (unrelated) 'Selberg class', a namesake collision with no bearing on the eigenvalue conjecture; and arXiv:2505.00653 (An, 'On the exponents of distribution of primes and smooth numbers', 2025) explicitly removes a *dependency* on Selberg's eigenvalue conjecture from prior conditional results (via new large sieve inequalities for exceptional Maass forms), making those specific prime/smooth-number-distribution results unconditional — but it does not touch, improve, or restate the conjecture's own status, so under §3.1 this is a related result about consequences of the conjecture, not a change to the bullet itself. I also found an active and distinct line of work (Wu-Xue, Lipnowski-Wright, Shen-Wu, 2021-2025) proving that Weil-Petersson-random compact hyperbolic surfaces of large genus have spectral gap approaching 1/4 with high probability. This is a genuinely different problem — a probabilistic/geometric question about random surfaces, not an arithmetic question about congruence subgroups and Maass forms — and per §3.1 counts as a related problem (a variant posed over different objects), not a case of the stated conjecture, so it does not change this record's status. No AI system was found anywhere near any of this work.
competing_reading: One could argue the random-hyperbolic-surfaces spectral-gap results (Wu-Xue et al.) are close enough in spirit — same numerical target (1/4), same type of eigenvalue question — to be treated as informative context, but they concern a different mathematical object (random Weil-Petersson metrics on topological surfaces) rather than a restriction of the stated problem (arithmetic congruence subgroups), so I classify them as out of scope rather than as `partial` progress.
what_would_settle_it: A paper or preprint that explicitly improves on the 975/4096 bound for the smallest exceptional eigenvalue of congruence subgroups (or proves the full 1/4 conjecture), or an update to the Kim-Sarnak record itself, would settle this. None was found in this search.
